why: P3 because it solves a real but narrow pain point, losing an unbroadcast private-broadcast transaction on node restart, for users of the still-experimental privatebroadcast feature.

Reviewers flagged a more valuable direction (a broadcast pool with scheduled/decoy transactions per craigraw) that the author is now pursuing separately in #34707, reducing the leverage of reviewing this specific implementation.

result.summary: This PR adds persistence for the private-broadcast feature: transactions that have been submitted via sendrawtransaction but not yet fully broadcast are dumped to a new privatebroadcast.dat file on shutdown and reloaded on startup, so they aren't lost if the node restarts mid-broadcast. It includes serialization/deserialization helpers, init-time load/dump logic gated by -privatebroadcast, a fuzz target, and functional test coverage.
result.problem: Currently, transactions queued for private broadcast live only in memory in the peer manager; if the node restarts before broadcast completes, the transaction is silently lost, which matters to operators and applications relying on sendrawtransaction with privatebroadcast=1.

open_concerns: tankyleo raised that persisting broadcast transaction data to disk changes the risk profile for non-wallet, broadcast-only nodes; author responded with mitigations (0600 permissions suggested by vasild, decoy transactions, early file removal) but no code change was made to address this fully.

craigraw argued this PR's approach is too narrow and that a broadcast-pool design (handling fee-driven mempool eviction and scheduled broadcast) would deliver much more value; author agreed and said '#34329 should be merged first' and later opened #34707 pursuing that direction instead.
resolved_concerns: Dependency on #34329 was resolved: it merged 2026-02-19.

categories.rationale: P3 because it addresses a real but narrow problem, a submitted private-broadcast transaction being lost on node restart, which matters to operators running privatebroadcast=1 but is a niche, opt-in feature. Reviewer craigraw noted 'losing broadcasted transactions due to a node restart is probably quite rare' compared to the broader broadcast-pool use case he'd prefer, and the author has since pivoted to pursuing that broader design in a separate PR (#34707), reducing this PR's standalone leverage.

uncertainties: Unclear whether this PR will be continued, closed in favor of #34707, or rebased once #34707's design direction is settled.
Whether the security concern about persisting sensitive broadcast data to disk (raised by tankyleo) would need a concrete fix (e.g., file permissions, encryption) before merge is undetermined.
result.card: This draft PR persists in-flight private-broadcast transactions to a privatebroadcast.dat file so they survive a node restart, addressing transaction loss for the opt-in privatebroadcast=1 feature. Two reviewers gave Concept ACKs, but vasild raised a security concern about persisting sensitive broadcast data to disk and craigraw argued the design should instead be a broader broadcast-pool feature (also referencing feature requests #30471 and #34118); the author agreed the broadcast-pool idea is preferable and opened a separate PR, #34707, pursuing that direction, then went silent for over six months. The PR is currently draft, marked needs-rebase, and its own author's pivot suggests this specific approach may be superseded. Depends on #34329 (merged 2026-02-19). Priority is modest: the underlying restart-data-loss problem is real but narrow and opt-in, and reviewer sentiment favors a different, more valuable design.
